claims.value: B cell receptors: thousands of membrane-bound immunoglobulin (antibody) molecules coating the surface of the naive cell
claims.quote: Similar to T cells, naïve B cells initially are coated in thousands of B cell receptors (BCRs), which are membrane-bound forms of Ig (immunoglobulin, or an antibody).

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: B cell receptor built from two heavy chains and two light chains joined by disulfide linkages
claims.quote: The B cell receptor has two heavy chains and two light chains connected by disulfide linkages.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: surface IgM and IgD (both receptor classes on mature B cells leaving the bone marrow, with the same antigen specificity)
claims.quote: Mature B cells that leave the bone marrow express both IgM and IgD, but both antibodies have the same antigen specificity.

source.section: 21.4 The Adaptive Immune Response: B-lymphocytes and Antibodies
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Ig alpha and Ig beta: two further membrane proteins, involved in signaling
claims.quote: Two other membrane proteins, Ig alpha and Ig beta, are involved in signaling.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: MHC class II molecules that display processed antigen to Th2 helper T cells
claims.quote: They bind and engulf foreign antigens via their BCRs and then display processed antigens in the context of MHC II molecules to TH2 cells.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Unlike a T cell, a B cell recognizes native, unprocessed antigen without needing MHC molecules or antigen-presenting cells.
claims.quote: B cells do not recognize antigen in the complex fashion of T cells. B cells can recognize native, unprocessed antigen and do not require the participation of MHC molecules and antigen-presenting cells.

source.section: 21.4 The Adaptive Immune Response: B-lymphocytes and Antibodies
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A B cell binds intact antigen because the antibodies it secretes must recognize the pathogen itself rather than digested remnants of it.
claims.quote: B cells must be able to bind intact antigens because they secrete antibodies that must recognize the pathogen directly, rather than digested remnants of the pathogen.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Each surface antibody has two binding sites, so an antigen with repeated units can crosslink the receptors, which is enough to activate the B cell without T cell cytokines.
claims.quote: Each antibody on the B cell surface has two binding sites, and the repeated nature of T cell-independent antigen leads to crosslinking of the surface antibodies on the B cell. The crosslinking is enough to activate it in the absence of T cell cytokines.

source.section: 21.4 The Adaptive Immune Response: B-lymphocytes and Antibodies
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It internalizes antigen caught by its surface antibody and presents processed pieces on class II MHC to Th2 helper cells, whose cytokines then complete its activation.
claims.quote: Some of this antigen is internalized, processed, and presented to the Th2 cells on a class II MHC molecule. The T cell then binds using its antigen receptor and is activated to secrete cytokines that diffuse to the B cell, finally activating it completely.

source.section: 21.4 The Adaptive Immune Response: B-lymphocytes and Antibodies
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: All the receptors on one B cell are identical, but different B cells carry different recognition domains, so the population as a whole can bind a very wide range of molecular structures.
claims.quote: The receptors of any particular B cell, as shown in are all the same, but the hundreds of millions of different B cells in an individual have distinct recognition domains that contribute to extensive diversity in the types of molecular structures to which they can bind.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
